title.jcr:title: Ambarella Products: SoCs, CPUs, Chipsets, and More

text_1.text: Ambarella’s technologies make cameras smarter - enabling features like person detection, object classification, analytics, and more - performing complex data analysis in real time, delivering breathtaking imagery, and preserving vital system resources such as power and network bandwidth. Ambarella specializes in the development of deployable, scalable designs for intelligent cameras, offering a proven path to mass production. Check out our Ambarella products, SoCs, CPUs, chipsets, and more.

text_2.text:
What is Ambarella CVflow architecture?

CVflow is Ambarella’s computer vision chip architecture. Unlike a general-purpose CPU or GPU, it uses a dedicated vision processing engine programmed with a high-level algorithm description. That design scales performance to trillions of operations per second at very low power.

Which neural network frameworks do Ambarella SoCs support?

Customers map CNNs trained with industry-standard tools such as Caffe, TensorFlow, and PyTorch onto Ambarella processors. The CNN toolkit also covers ONNX. Detection, classification, and related CNN/DNN tasks run on-chip.

Which Ambarella SoCs are used for ADAS?

CV2FS is for front-facing stereovision ADAS cameras and computer-vision ECUs at L2+ and higher, with CVflow AI and ASIL C compliance. CV22FS targets forward-facing monocular ADAS cameras and similar ECUs, also with ASIL C. Ambarella uses ISO 26262 processes for functional safety–certified products used in ADAS and autonomous driving.

What makes Ambarella a low-power edge AI SoC choice?

The SoCs and CPUs are built for embedded edge platforms such as battery-powered cameras. They can outperform competing solutions on power efficiency, sometimes by 5× or more, while matching or beating results. Compression also cuts bandwidth and storage.

What does stereovision add for robotics?

Stereo processing turns a 2D view into a 3D scene and can detect generic obstacles the system was not trained to recognize. CV2 is positioned for accurate 3D environmental modeling, real-time neural network performance, advanced robotics, and industrial autonomous robots.

heading_1.jcr:title: Ambarella N1 Family - Edge GenAI Is Here

text_3.text:
Ambarella’s N1 family of Edge GenAI SoCs delivers the processing power needed to run multimodal large language models (LLMs), vision-language models (VLMs), and traditional CNN networks locally, without cloud dependency. Designed for autonomous mobile robots, on-premise AI boxes, smart city security, industrial automation, and intelligent healthcare, the N1 series sets a new benchmark for AI performance per watt at the edge.

As an authorized Ambarella distributor and value-added engineering partner, Macnica Americas provides component supply, design-in support, and technical consulting to help you bring your next N1-based design to production.

text_4.text:
CVflow® Chip Architecture

Ambarella CVflow® chip architecture is based on a deep understanding of core computer vision algorithms. Unlike general-purpose CPUs and GPUs, CVflow includes a dedicated vision processing engine programmed with a high-level algorithm description, allowing Ambarella architecture to scale performance to trillions of operations per second with extremely low power consumption.

With CVflow, customers can efficiently map their own CNN networks trained with industry-standard tools (e.g., Caffe, TensorFlow, PyTorch) to run on Ambarella processors.

text_5.text:
Stereovision

Stereo processing transforms the world from a flat 2D plane into a full 3D environment. This not only provides a richer, denser representation of the target scene, but also allows the detection of generic obstacles that the system hasn’t been trained to recognize, making navigation safer and more effective for warehouse robots, autonomous vehicles, and more.

text_6.text:
Low Power

Ambarella technology products are designed to be deployed in embedded platforms on the edge (e.g., battery-powered cameras), where power consumption is a critical concern. Ambarella SoCs and CPUs consistently outperform competitive solutions in power efficiency - sometimes by 5x or more - while delivering equal or superior results.

text_7.text:
Reduce Bandwidth & Storage Costs

Ambarella compression technologies dramatically reduce data transmission size, slashing storage costs and bandwidth usage with Ambarella products.

text_8.text:
Image Quality

One of the hallmarks of Ambarella processors is our image processing pipeline. Encompassing everything from HDR to EIS to dewarping, our state-of-the-art ISP ensures that every frame of every video is exquisite, improving safety and enhancing the viewing experience.

text_9.text:
Autonomy

From drones to robots, from taxis to long-haul semi trucks, Ambarella’s vision processors were designed to revolutionize the way we work and travel. Our hardware platforms deliver the flexibility required to implement all levels of automation, including partial, conditional, high, and full autonomy.

text_10.text:
Functional Safety

As an AI silicon company offering SoCs for applications such as ADAS and autonomous driving, Ambarella has implemented an array of internal processes and procedures to ensure that their functional safety-certified products comply with ISO 26262. These strict processes and procedures touch every aspect of the work Ambarella does - from technical documentation to software engineering to VLSI - and have become an inextricable part of Ambarella culture, from top to bottom.

title.jcr:title: Altera Agilex 7 FPGA and SoC Overview

text_1.text: The Altera Agilex 7 devices include the industry’s highest performance FPGAs providing a range of premium features for the most demanding applications, including the F-Series, I-Series, and M-Series. This tier offers the industry’s highest data rate transceivers - up to 116 Gbps - the first PCIe 5.0 and CXL support, and options to integrate in-package HBM2E memory delivering the industry’s highest memory bandwidth (over 1 TBps). These capabilities enable customized connectivity and acceleration for the most compute, bandwidth, and memory-intensive use cases in communications, data center, defense, high-performance computing, video, high-end test/measurement/medical, and more.

I-Series devices offer the highest performance I/O interfaces to address bandwidth-intensive applications. Manufactured on Altera 10 nm SuperFin process technology, this series builds upon the F-Series device features offering transceiver rates up to 116 Gbps, PCIe 5.0 support, and cache- and memory-coherent attach to processors with CXL. M-Series devices are optimized for compute and memory-intensive applications. heading_5.jcr:title: Design Gateway Industries and Use Cases

text_5.text: Move large datasets between accelerators and storage with predictable latency and minimal CPU load. Use TOE100G or TOE200G with UDP100G for transport, pair with NVMe-IP or muNVMe-IP for storage on Agilex 7.

text_6.text: Hit tight-latency targets for order flow, feed handling, and audit logging. Use Design Gateway's TOE10G or TOE25G with the Low Latency EMAC, add tCAM-IP for filtering and NVMe-IP for capture, target Agilex 5 for appliances or Agilex 7 for 100G aggregation.

text_7.text: Feed encoders and recorders reliably and keep long recordings steady without CPU tuning. Use UDP10G or UDP25G for media streams with TOE10G for control, combine with NVMe-IP for recording on Agilex 5, move to Agilex 7 for 100G hubs.

text_8.text: Move high frame rate image data into processing chains with deterministic timing. Use UDP10G or UDP25G with the low-latency EMAC, add NVMe-IP for burst buffers, deploy on Agilex 5 E-Series.

heading_10.jcr:title: Edge data logging and test instrumentation

text_9.text: Sustain continuous high speed capture in compact enclosures. Use NVMe-IP for steady writes and raNVMe-IP for random access logs, target Agilex 5.

text_10.text: Scale packet processing and stateful transport while keeping CPU usage low. Use TOE25G or TOE100G with UDP25G or UDP100G, add TLS1.3-IP and AES-GCM for security, select Agilex 7 for core and Agilex 5 for edge.

text_11.text: Move video and sensor telemetry at the edge with consistent throughput. Use UDP10G or UDP25G with the low-latency EMAC, add NVMe-IP for evidence buffers and AES-GCM for secure transport, target Agilex 5.

text_1.text:
Physical AI Starts Where the World Moves.

AI is leaving the data center. The next phase of AI is Physical AI, intelligence embedded directly into machines, robots, and systems that must sense, decide, and act in the real world, in real time. Macnica enables Physical AI systems by combining advanced sensing, efficient on-device AI processing powered by DeepX, and deterministic communication into deployable, production-ready solutions.

heading_1.jcr:title: Why Traditional AI Architectures Break Down in the Physical World

text_1.text:
Most AI infrastructure was designed for centralized computing. GPUs, cloud platforms, and data centers excel at training and large-scale analytics, but they struggle when intelligence must operate continuously in the physical world.

Physical AI systems face constraints that cloud-based AI cannot solve:

  • Latency that impacts safety, responsiveness, and autonomy
  • Power and thermal limits inside robots, machines, and edge devices
  • Connectivity gaps and unreliable networks
  • GPU supply constraints and long lead times
  • Rising infrastructure and energy costs

When AI must interact with people, environments, and machines, intelligence cannot depend on distant servers or power-hungry infrastructure.

Physical AI demands a fundamentally different system architecture.

heading_1.jcr:title: The Final Stage of AI Is Physical

text_1.text:
Physical AI is the integration of intelligent models with embodied systems that operate in the real world. It closes the loop between perception, reasoning, and action.

Instead of sending data to the cloud for processing, Physical AI runs inference where action happens, on the device, at the edge, within tight power, latency, and reliability constraints.

In practical terms:

  • AI sees through sensors
  • AI decides using on-device intelligence
  • AI acts through machines and systems

This shift transforms AI from an analytical tool into an operational capability.

Physical AI systems cannot wait for the cloud.

They require intelligence that runs locally, predictably, and efficiently, even when connectivity is limited or unavailable.

On-device AI processing enables:

  • Consistent performance within fixed power and thermal envelopes
  • Reduced reliance on constrained GPU supply chains
  • Scalable deployment across fleets of machines

DeepX accelerators are purpose-built for this reality, delivering high-performance AI inference within power budgets suitable for physical systems.

title.jcr:title: Altera Agilex 5 FPGA and SoC Overview

text_1.text: Altera Agilex 5 devices serve a broad range of applications that require high performance, lower power, and smaller form factors. This tier consists of the performance-optimized D-Series FPGAs and the power-optimized E-Series FPGAs. Altera Agilex 5 devices also feature the industry’s first Enhanced DSP with AI Tensor Block, which deliver high-efficiency AI and digital signal processing (DSP) functionality, and the FPGA industry’s first asymmetric applications processor system consisting of dual Arm Cortex-A76 cores and dual Cortex-A55 cores, which enable you to optimize the performance and power efficiency of their workloads. These characteristics make them ideal for midrange FPGA applications across the edge and core including wireless and wireline communications, video and broadcast equipment, industrial applications, test and measurement products, medical electronics, and defense applications.

table_1.text:
E-Series FPGAs and SoCs D-Series FPGAs and SoCs
E-Series FPGAs and SoCs are optimized for power and size - with 50% lower power while delivering up to 2.5X better performance as compared to Cyclone V devices, also with features including transceiver rates up to 24x28 Gbps, PCIe 4.0x4, 6x25GbE, 3,600 Mbps DDR5, dual core of A55 and dual core of A76 make it ideal for intelligent applications at the edge, embedded, and more. D-Series FPGAs and SoCs are optimized for performance and power efficiency - with 42% lower power while delivering up to 1.5X better performance as compared to Stratix 10 FPGAs, also with features including transceiver rates up to 32x28 Gbps, PCIe 4.0x8, 16x25GbE, 4,000 Mbps DDR5, dual core of A55 and dual core of A76 make it ideal for various applications across multiple markets.

text_2.text:
What is the difference between Agilex 5 E-Series and D-Series?

E-Series is optimized for power and size: 50% lower power and up to 2.5× better performance than Cyclone V, transceivers to 24×28 Gbps, and PCIe 4.0 x4. D-Series is optimized for performance: 42% lower power and up to 1.5× better performance than Stratix 10, transceivers to 32×28 Gbps, and PCIe 4.0 x8.

What is the AI Tensor Block in Agilex 5?

Agilex 5 includes an Enhanced DSP with AI Tensor Block for high-efficiency AI and DSP. Peak INT8 throughput reaches 25.99 TOPS on the E-Series A5E 065A and 56.22 TOPS on the D-Series A5D 064, with variable-precision DSP blocks.

What processors are in the Agilex 5 hard processor system?

The SoC uses an asymmetric applications processor: dual Arm Cortex-A76 cores up to 1.8 GHz and dual Cortex-A55 cores up to 1.5 GHz, with up to 2 MB shared L3 cache. That pairing balances performance and power by workload.

Which memory and interface standards does Agilex 5 support?

DDR5 to 4,000 Mbps on D-Series and 3,600 Mbps on E-Series, plus DDR4, LPDDR4, and LPDDR5. Connectivity includes PCIe 4.0, up to 6×25GbE on E-Series and 16×25GbE on D-Series, MIPI D-PHY, LVDS at 1.6 Gbps, and TSN.

What applications is the Agilex 5 mid-range FPGA aimed at?

Midrange edge and core designs: wireless and wireline communications, video and broadcast, industrial, test and measurement, medical electronics, and defense. Named focus markets are image sensor processing, autonomous mobile robots, and clinical systems, including battery-powered clinical equipment.

text_1.text: Manufacturing is entering a new era where robotics, machine vision, and AI operate continuously across the factory floor. Building intelligent robots for industrial environments is not just a software problem. It is a system challenge involving perception, real-time decision making, power constraints, and reliable connectivity. Macnica helps robotics developers design edge AI architectures that enable robots and intelligent machines to operate reliably in Smart Factory environments. Using our Capture → Process → Communicate philosophy, we combine advanced sensing, efficient on-device AI processing powered by DeepX, and deterministic communication to enable autonomous robotics at scale.

heading_1.jcr:title: Robotics as the Foundation of the Smart Factory

text_1.text:
Smart factories are built on networks of intelligent machines that continuously monitor, analyze, and optimize industrial operations.

These environments rely heavily on robotics systems, such as:

  • Autonomous mobile robots moving materials
  • Machine vision systems inspecting production lines
  • Intelligent logistics platforms coordinating warehouse operations
  • Robotics systems assisting workers safely on the factory floor

Edge AI plays a critical role in enabling these systems to operate safely and efficiently.

Smart factories rely on AI-powered automation, predictive maintenance, and quality control, where machines continuously analyze their environment and adapt to changing conditions.

text_1.text:
Factory robots must respond instantly to changing conditions.

That means AI must run inside the robot or machine, not in distant data centers.

Edge AI enables robotics systems to:

  • Process multiple sensors simultaneously: Robots combine cameras, LiDAR, and other sensors to understand their environment.
  • Make real-time decisions: Navigation, obstacle detection, and task coordination require millisecond response times.
  • Operate reliably without cloud dependence: Factories cannot tolerate interruptions caused by connectivity issues.
  • Run within tight power budgets: Battery-powered robots must operate efficiently to maximize uptime.

These requirements make on-device AI processing essential for industrial robotics.

title.jcr:title: i-Chips Scaler LSI (Large Scale Integration) Circuits

text_1.text: i-Chips Scaler LSI (Large-Scale Integration), revolutionizes electronic devices by integrating numerous electronic components and functions onto a single chip. This advanced technology enables significant miniaturization and improved performance. In the context of video processing, the term "scaler" refers to the integrated circuit's capability to perform scaling or resizing functions. Found in TVs, monitors, projectors, and video processors, i-Chips Scaler LSIs convert incoming video signals to different resolutions, ensuring compatibility with various display formats. By leveraging sophisticated algorithms and signal processing techniques, i-Chips Scaler LSI large scale integration circuits analyze and modify video signals, upscaling or downscaling them to match the desired resolution or aspect ratio of the display device. Additionally, these chips may undertake additional tasks like deinterlacing, color space conversion, and noise reduction. i-Chips Scaler LSIs help in achieving optimal picture quality and seamless compatibility across different video sources and displays. They empower users to enjoy diverse video formats and resolutions on devices with varying display capabilities, providing an immersive visual experience.

heading_1.jcr:title: DEEPX NPU Architecture Built Around Power, Thermal, and Precision

text_2.text: GPUs overheat in sealed enclosures, low-power NPUs cannot sustain production frame rates on real detection models, and cloud inference introduces round-trip latency and data egress that industrial and safety-critical systems cannot tolerate. DEEPX NPU architecture is designed specifically around these failure modes, with power envelope, thermal characteristics, and quantization fidelity treated as primary design constraints rather than secondary considerations. All performance claims are independently benchmarked against production workloads.

text_3.text: The DEEPX IQ8 quantization engine addresses the precision trade-off that limits most edge NPU deployments. Standard INT8 quantization reduces memory bandwidth and compute requirements but introduces accuracy degradation that requires per-layer calibration to recover. IQ8 performs INT8-width computation while preserving the numerical range of FP32 inference, delivering full-speed throughput without model accuracy loss and without manual calibration. For teams deploying YOLO-family or custom detection models, this removes a significant pre-production engineering step.

text_4.text: Thermal performance is validated in direct hardware comparison. Running identical workloads, the DX-M1 board surface measured 35.5 degrees C versus 60.7 degrees C for a competing chip. In sealed enclosures without active cooling, that 25-degree delta is the margin between a qualified fanless design and one that requires thermal redesign or derating at operating temperature.

The DX-M Series are bare chips and M.2 modules for embedding directly into host systems: robots, cameras, vehicles, and edge devices. The DX-H Series are low-profile PCIe cards for servers and workstations running multi-channel video analytics and AI inference at scale.
